comments.body:
First plan review BLOCKed with one blocking finding (E4) and two advisories. All three were correct.

The blocking finding: the census omitted `tests/unit/workflow/test_review_skeleton.py` (lines 104, 117), so AC7's promised four-path residue was wrong. Root cause is a sequencing error on my part, not a miscount — slice 9 (`9b96-18b7-b19e-4f85`) repoints that file onto `spec-alignment`, and I took the census on slice 9's tree while plan review pins material at `origin/main`, which does not yet carry slice 9. The reviewer was reading the real tree and I was reading a future one.

Fix: added an explicit Ordering section naming slice 9 as a hard predecessor and stating what a tree-wide grep reports until it lands. The census itself is unchanged and correct for the post-slice-9 tree.

Advisory 1 (COH/E1): the summary said "no documentation changes" while AC4/AC6 require a `docs/release-notes.md` addition. Summary reworded to carve the release-note entry out explicitly, and the out-of-scope paragraph now explains that release-notes' *existing* `ticket-quality` mentions are left alone because the file is historical narrative.

Advisory 2 (P6, DET, minor): the ACs used a `$F7` shell variable inside the grep and pytest commands, which expands before the command runs, so the written pattern is not what executes. Every AC now spells the seven paths out literally, and AC3 describes the collect-and-sort pipeline in prose rather than embedding `grep '::'`.

Re-review is deliberately deferred until slice 9 is on `origin/main`; re-running it before then would reproduce the same blocking finding against the same unchanged tree.

comments.body:
Closing as a duplicate of slice 8 (`d4ca-0470-d792-49df`, `flammable-corrupting-pipit`), which was already committed when this ticket was filed.

Slice 8's commit — "Repoint stand-in tests off ticket-quality", now Gerrit 3143 — makes byte-identical changes to the same seven files: 25 lines, `ticket-quality` → `code-quality`, with `ticket_quality` → `code_quality` in the one filename spelling. `git diff --numstat` for slice 8 is 1/1, 1/1, 3/3, 1/1, 7/7, 8/8, 4/4 across exactly the paths this ticket's Context enumerates.

Root cause of the duplicate: the census that produced this ticket was run on slice 9's worktree, which is `origin/main` plus slice 9 only. Slice 8 was committed on its own branch and still unlanded, so its 25 substitutions were invisible to the census and I re-derived them as new work. The same blind spot produced this ticket's plan-review BLOCK from the opposite direction — there the census saw slice 9's repoint that `origin/main` did not have.

The lesson is one rule, not two: census against the union of `origin/main` and every committed-but-unlanded slice branch, not against whichever single worktree is open.

The investigation was not wasted. It independently proved slice 8's change correct before slice 8's own `make verify` finished — 110 passed across the six locally-runnable files and 116 collected node IDs byte-identical to `origin/main` — and it proved the deletion that follows: with the repoint plus the prompt deleted, the index regenerated, and both rosters shrunk, 937 passed and 9 skipped with no failures. That deletion is filed as slice 11.

No code from this ticket was written, so there is no commit and no file impact to retire.

compiled_state.description:
Slice 10 of epic 87d8. Repoints the seven remaining test files that use the
`ticket-quality` reviewer prompt onto `code-quality`, so the next slice can delete
the prompt without breaking them. The only non-test change is a release-note entry.
The prompt still exists after this slice, so every repointed test passes both before
and after, which is what makes this slice independently verifiable.

## Ordering

This slice must land after slice 9 (`9b96-18b7-b19e-4f85`), which repoints
`tests/unit/workflow/test_review_skeleton.py` (lines 104 and 117) onto
`spec-alignment`. That file is not in this slice's scope and is not counted in the
census below, which is taken on top of slice 9. Until slice 9 is on `main`, a
tree-wide `ticket-quality` grep reports it as an eighth test file and AC7's residual
list is short by one path.

## Context

Epic 87d8 is retiring the `ticket-quality` reviewer prompt. Slices 1-9 cleared it out
of the engine, the workflow example, the variant/override tests, and the framework
docs. A census with

    git grep -cF -e 'ticket-quality' -e 'ticket_quality' -- src tests

run on slice 9's tree finds the prompt file itself, its generated `index.json` entry,
and nine test files. Two of those nine are roster enumerations that must shrink when
the prompt is deleted; they belong to the next slice. The other seven use
`ticket-quality` as a stand-in for *some* real packaged reviewer, and are this
slice's subject:

- `tests/external/test_pydantic_ai_cutover_live.py` (1 hit, line 181)
- `tests/interfaces/store/test_agent_op_safeguard.py` (1 hit, line 86)
- `tests/interfaces/store/test_llm_framework.py` (3 hits, lines 48, 49, 59)
- `tests/unit/test_generated_surface_markers.py` (1 hit, line 130)
- `tests/unit/test_prompt_index.py` (7 hits, lines 17, 18, 22, 29, 30, 32, 36)
- `tests/unit/test_prompt_library_writes.py` (8 hits, lines 48, 49, 50, 76, 94, 100,
  101, 109)
- `tests/unit/test_prompts_git_canonical.py` (4 hits, lines 18, 25, 30, 57)

None of these tests is about `ticket-quality`. They assert resolver behaviour,
catalog membership, library enumeration, user-override precedence, and canonical
round-tripping, and each needs a real packaged reviewer to assert it against.

Three artifact classes are deliberately out of scope, as in every prior slice of this
epic: `evals/plan-review-gate/runs/*.jsonl` (frozen corpora), and the tracked
`.test_durations` (a pytest-split cache that ignores unknown node IDs and regenerates
itself; never hand-edited). `docs/release-notes.md` is historical narrative, so its
existing `ticket-quality` mentions are likewise left alone — this slice only prepends
a new entry to it.

## Why `code-quality`

The substitute must satisfy every property the seven files assert. `code-quality`
matches `ticket-quality` on all of them:

- `category: review`, so `is_reviewer` is True and `enumerate_criteria()` excludes it
  (`test_prompt_library_writes.py:109` asserts that exclusion).
- `inputs: reviewer_input`, `outputs: review_result`, `execution_mode: agentic`.
- `dimension` equal to its own id, which `test_prompt_index.py:22` asserts.
- The same two template variables, `{{ticket_id}}` and `{{ticket_context}}`.
  `test_prompts_git_canonical.py:30` depends on there being two, because it omits one
  and expects a raise.
- No `applies_to` globs, so `select_reviewers` behaviour is unchanged.
- Packaged and not an overlay, which `test_prompt_library_writes.py:48-50` asserts.
- It survives the epic.

The other four catalog reviewers do not. `security` and `tests` declare `applies_to`
globs. `spec-alignment` takes `{{spec}}` and `{{epics}}`, not `{{ticket_id}}`.
`completion-verifier` is not interchangeable with a general reviewer.

None of the seven files mentions `code-quality` today, so the substitution introduces
no duplicate or self-shadowing id.

## Change

A single literal substitution in the seven files: `ticket-quality` becomes
`code-quality`, and the one `ticket_quality` filename spelling becomes `code_quality`.
Twenty-five lines change in total. Comments that name the prompt change with it, so
`test_prompts_git_canonical.py:30` still describes the prompt it actually exercises.
One entry is prepended to `docs/release-notes.md`.

No assertion, test name, parametrize list, or test count changes. The string appears
only inside test bodies and module-level dicts, never in a parametrize argument, so
the collected node IDs are identical before and after.

## Testing

No new tests. This slice changes which existing reviewer the existing tests assert
against, and the proof it is correct is that all of them still pass unchanged. The
seven files were run together with the substitution applied: 110 passed in the six
selectable files, and the collected node IDs across all seven (116) are
byte-identical to the same collection without the substitution.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **AC1** This command prints nothing and exits 1:
      `git grep -cF -e 'ticket-quality' -e 'ticket_quality' --
      tests/external/test_pydantic_ai_cutover_live.py
      tests/interfaces/store/test_agent_op_safeguard.py
      tests/interfaces/store/test_llm_framework.py
      tests/unit/test_generated_surface_markers.py tests/unit/test_prompt_index.py
      tests/unit/test_prompt_library_writes.py
      tests/unit/test_prompts_git_canonical.py`.
      Before this slice it prints 1, 1, 3, 1, 7, 8 and 4.
- [ ] **AC2** `pytest tests/interfaces/store/test_agent_op_safeguard.py
      tests/interfaces/store/test_llm_framework.py
      tests/unit/test_generated_surface_markers.py tests/unit/test_prompt_index.py
      tests/unit/test_prompt_library_writes.py
      tests/unit/test_prompts_git_canonical.py -q` exits 0 and its last line is
      `110 passed`.
- [ ] **AC3** Collecting those six files plus
      `tests/external/test_pydantic_ai_cutover_live.py` with
      `pytest ... -q --collect-only`, keeping lines containing a double colon and
      sorting them, yields 116 node IDs byte-identical to the same collection on
      `origin/main`.
- [ ] **AC4** `git diff --numstat origin/main...HEAD` lists exactly those seven test
      files plus `docs/release-notes.md`, and no other path.
- [ ] **AC5** `ruff check src tests docs` exits 0 with no output.
- [ ] **AC6** `git diff --numstat origin/main...HEAD -- docs/release-notes.md` shows a
      non-zero addition count and `0` deletions.
- [ ] **AC7** `git grep -cF -e 'ticket-quality' -e 'ticket_quality' -- src tests`
      reports hits in exactly four paths:
      `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/index.json`,
      `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/ticket_quality.md`,
      `tests/unit/test_prompt_cache_split.py` and
      `tests/unit/test_prompt_front_matter.py`. This is the hand-off to the next
      slice, which deletes all four.
- [ ] **AC8** `make verify` exits 0.
